:::{#rem-cv-estimate}
#### What the cross-validation estimate estimates

Each prediction in @eq-cv-estimate comes from a rule
that did not see the observation it predicts,
so each squared error is scored as in @thm-held-out-unbiased.
But the rule for fold $\fold{\ifold}$ was fitted to $\nobs - \foldsize{\ifold}$ observations,
not $\nobs$,
and the $\nfolds$ rules differ from one another and from the rule fitted to all $\nobs$.
So $\cvest{\nfolds}$ estimates the [expected generalization error](#def-expected-generalization-error)
of the fitting *procedure* $\fitproc$ at the smaller training-set sizes $\nobs - \foldsize{\ifold}$,
which is $\expgenerr{\fitproc}{\nobs (\nfolds - 1) / \nfolds}$ when every fold has $\nobs / \nfolds$ observations,
rather than $\generr_{\trainset}$ for the one rule fitted to all the data
[@hastie2009elements, sec. 7.12].

When every [fold](#def-folds) has $\foldsize{\ifold} = \nobs / \nfolds$ observations,
$\cvest{\nfolds}$ is also the average of the $\nfolds$ [fold mean squared errors](#def-fold-mse)
$\foldmse{1}, \ldots, \foldmse{\nfolds}$,
the form @james2021islr2e [sec. 5.1.3] use.

:::
